Hash A is the committed docs/usage.md (git rev-parse HEAD:docs/usage.md). The documentation record's checks and the final-deliverable review's assessed inputs and conclusion name only blob A.

Hash B is the unstaged working-tree docs/usage.md (git hash-object docs/usage.md). It changes the check example from `python3 -m tally check data/expenses.csv` to `python3 -m tally check --strict data/expenses.csv`, adds a sentence about --strict, and adds an exit status 1 bullet. No Documenter check, documentation record entry, or review covers B.

B's statements are supported by tally/__main__.py (--strict exists and exits 1 on rows with a blank category), so B is not known to be wrong; the problem is that the current guide has no current Documenter evidence and the final review no longer applies to it.
Nothing in the repository records who made the B edit; it is within the docs/usage.md editing boundary.

Documenter is the earliest included owner whose evidence is stale (a DOCUMENTATION failure to DOCUMENTING with ResumeAt SYNCHRONIZING); final review must then be re-established for the current guide before synchronization can pass.

notes: Standalone Brownfield DOCUMENTATION cycle for a small Python CLI (tally). The runner has python3 but no python command, so the project's docs, records, and selfChecks all use python3. 00-project (pre-install): code, tests, sample data, and an old short docs/usage.md. 50-cycle: CONTEXT.md, scope (AC-001..AC-003), Architect's existing-contract design, and STATE at DOCUMENTING. 55-guide: docs/usage.md version A, committed alone so later BLOB references resolve to A. 60-doc-record: a COMPLETE documentation record whose checks cite ${BLOB:docs/usage.md} (A) and the guide commit; STATE at REVIEWING_FINAL. 65-final-review: a COMPLETE FINAL_DELIVERABLE review with no findings, citing blob A and the documentation record blob; STATE at SYNCHRONIZING via FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL. 70-guide-edit: unstaged docs/usage.md version B (the check example now uses --strict, plus an exit status 1 bullet). B is accurate to the code, so the issue is only that the evidence is stale. No synchronization record exists yet. The date is set so commits follow the cycle ID timestamp.
